meta.note: Scores are analyst estimates for interface testing. Source claims require verification before executive use.

signals.title: Reduced precipitation increases near-term operating sensitivity
signals.change: Canal operating measures are being adjusted in response to below-expected watershed precipitation.
signals.impact: Water availability remains a first-order operating constraint because freshwater supports both Canal operations and human consumption.
signals.action: Track watershed precipitation, lake levels, draft/slot notices and any acceleration in restrictions. Treat water as a standing executive variable rather than an episodic climate story.

foda.threat: Lower water availability can constrain capacity and increase volatility.
foda.opportunity: Clear scarcity management can reinforce operational credibility if communicated transparently.

sources.name: Panama Canal Authority
sources.note: Primary operational source; verify current advisory/notice.

signals.title: Hormuz disruption keeps global maritime routing under pressure
signals.change: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains materially disrupted amid renewed regional conflict.
signals.impact: Energy prices, insurance, voyage economics and alternative routing can shift quickly. Any Panama Canal traffic benefit is a hypothesis—not an automatic consequence—and must be tested against actual route economics and booking data.
signals.action: Separate the verified disruption from the Panama-routing hypothesis. Watch tanker/container flows, Cape rerouting, Suez/Red Sea conditions, bunker costs and Canal booking patterns for evidence of a Panama effect.

foda.threat: Higher energy and security costs can reshape trade and amplify geopolitical scrutiny of chokepoints.
foda.opportunity: Some route shifts could improve the relative value of reliable Canal transit, if operational capacity is available.

sources.name: Reuters
sources.note: Independent confirmation layer; verify current September 1 dispatches.

signals.title: Constituent-assembly agenda remains an institutional watch item
signals.change: Political organization around an originaria constituent process remains visible in Panama's public agenda.
signals.impact: The strategic issue for the Canal is not constitutional debate in the abstract, but whether a future process could place the constitutional framework governing the Canal into political negotiation or create uncertainty around institutional safeguards.
signals.action: Monitor formal process milestones, coalition breadth, proposed scope, polling and statements specifically touching the Canal's constitutional title. Avoid treating the existence of the movement as proof that Canal provisions will change.

foda.threat: Institutional uncertainty could affect confidence if Canal governance becomes part of constitutional bargaining.
foda.opportunity: The Canal's performance and legitimacy can provide a reference point for institutional stability.

sources.name: SEPRESAC
sources.note: Primary/public process source; triangulate political significance independently.

signals.title: Donoso mine decision path retains social-mobilization potential
signals.change: Government deliberation over the future of the Donoso mining asset remains a potential trigger for renewed national debate.
signals.impact: A decision perceived as reopening settled constitutional or environmental questions could reactivate protest networks, affect logistics and reshape trust in institutions. A transparent process could instead reduce uncertainty.
signals.action: Watch official decision milestones, union/civic mobilization, court framing, environmental messaging and early protest coordination rather than waiting for street disruption.

foda.threat: National protests can spill into logistics, reputation and institutional narratives.
foda.opportunity: ACP neutrality, continuity and public-service credibility can become comparatively valuable during periods of national friction.
